title: Author Correction Selective manipulation of the inositol metabolic pathway for induction of salt-tolerance in indica ric

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section ('Analysis of homozygous transgenic lines') vs. Figure 3 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The main text states: 'Comparative shoot-length, root-length and fresh wt. taken after 10 days-stress indicated 7PcINO1-line, 10PcIMT1-line and 6DC1-line as the best in terms of growth parameters (Fig. 3a–c).' However, the caption for Figure 3 explicitly states that these phenotypic measurements (shoot-length, root-length, fresh-weight bar diagrams in panels a-c) were made on plants 'kept for 7 days' under variable NaCl stress. The stress duration stated in the main text (10 days) directly contradicts the duration given in the figure's own caption (7 days) for the same dataset (Fig. 3a–c).

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods/Results section describing Southern blot and segregation analysis
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'Homozygous T₂ lines ... were selected for Southern blot analysis of plants from PcINO1-lines (110 plants), PcIMT1-lines (153 plants) and ... DC1 (98 plants) lines,' explicitly identifying the Southern-blotted generation as T2. The very next sentence then refers to 'Southern positive T₃ PcINO1-plants exhibiting additional single-copy integration ... were used for segregation analysis,' switching the generational label to T3 without explanation. This creates an unresolved inconsistency as to which generation (T2 or T3) was actually subjected to Southern blot analysis versus advanced for segregation analysis.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph on inositol and cellular metabolism
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states: 'Depletion of inositol in the fungal, plant or animal system induces cell death termed as "inositol-less death"^12.' The term 'inositol-less death' is a well-established phenomenon specifically described and named in inositol-auxotrophic yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) strains; broadly extending this specific terminology to generic 'plant or animal' systems without further qualification or additional supporting citations is an overgeneralization that misrepresents the scope of the cited phenomenon.
